items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Well we had Jonathan Winters on the show one time

ctx.x: Well we had Jonathan Winters on the show one time, and you know Jonathan, right? Jonathan’s really out there. And the premise of this whole thing was, it was probably in July and we were doing a Christmas show. And the premise was that Jonathan had a clay piggy bank that he was returning. Steve Allen was behind the counter. And Steve came over the counter and he was next in line. And he said, “Yes sir.” And he said, “What’s wrong with that?” And all of a sudden Jonathan went — this is a Christmas show — went to…

Germany, wherever he went, they took eight minutes of what he was talking about and put it in six different shows. And all brilliant. All eight minutes of brilliance. Because Jonathan Winters is a monster mind. He’s out there, completely out there.

items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 5, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: if he did a comedy bit with Jonathan Winters and he wanted to use the band

ctx.x: And I admire that and so I wanted to talk about your TV band days. I’m imagining that that was a pressure situation. Like, okay Terry, tomorrow we’ve got this certain guest and they want this theme, and have it ready. Is that correct?

Well I’ll tell you how it all started. I used to be — Steve Allen was my friend. I was friends with Steve in the early 40s, late 40s. He became my friend then he became a big fan of mine, you know. And when he got his TV show he got me as a guest all the time, I was a guest a lot. And we were doing the show in California and I did his show with them and one of the producers, he loved me. He loved my dumb sense of humor, because I’m not a comedian but I’ve got the wit sort of like Steve’s. Steve loved me because,…

they said, “Okay we want you, it’s your job, but Steve Allen had a nine piece orchestra, we’ll give you a nine piece orchestra.” I said, “I don’t want it.” They said, “Well what do you mean?” I said, “You mean they give me a big band because we’re opposite Johnny Carson? Or opposite Elliot Lawrence who was with Les Crane — those shows at that time they all had 16 piece bands. And to me a 16 piece band — give me a sextet. I said sextet? Can you make it with a sextet? You see working with Steve Allen, of course I…
